h1:
Hua Hin Breakfast
Congee, Dim Sum, Chatchai Market & Old-School Coffee
intro: Mornings in Hua Hin give you plenty of reasons to get up before the sky is fully light — hot pork congee, fresh steamed dim sum, pa thong ko (Thai crullers) dunked in soy milk, and old-school coffee in weathered wooden shophouses. For a lot of people the starting point is Chatchai Market, the morning market in the center of town that has been part of Hua Hin for more than 80 years. We've picked out the spots locals actually go to, with opening times and rough prices.

blocks.html: Hua Hin rewards early risers. The morning food here mixes old Chinese cooking with Thai seaside street food, and many stalls have been run by the same families for generations — they often sell out before noon. The simple trick is to show up before 8am and graze your way through one neighborhood, one dish at a time.

Chatchai Market sits right in the center of Hua Hin, around Soi Hua Hin 72. It's an old morning market where locals and visitors both come to eat, with everything packed into one place: grilled pork skewers, sticky rice, pa thong ko, soy milk, roast duck, chicken rice and Thai sweets — all at local prices, and easy to graze through dish by dish. It's busiest from 6am to 8am.

items: Uncle Tae's Grilled Pork — pork skewers with sticky rice, around 10 THB a stick. A good snack to keep you going while you walk the market.
Tua Or Pa Thong Ko & Soy Milk — freshly fried Thai crullers dunked in warm soy milk, just a few baht per piece.
Hia Chai Roast Duck — roast duck and crispy pork over rice, starting around 12–15 THB, sold in the morning until it runs out.
Grandma's Kui Chai (chive cakes) — thin-skinned fried chive dumplings with a generous filling, a morning favorite people line up for.
Ko Uan Beef Noodles — chewy noodles in a beef broth, around 30 THB a bowl, 40 THB for the special.

blocks.title: How to Make It in Time
blocks.html: The good food at Chatchai Market tends to sell out fast — some of the famous stalls are gone before 9am. If you're coming specifically to eat, get there early and bring cash, since most stalls don't take cards or bank transfers.

blocks.title: Want to taste deeper? Try a Prachuap Khiri Khan food tour or cooking class
blocks.text: Half a day with a local who knows the lanes — or cooking a dish yourself — teaches you more than just eating. Book ahead on Klook or GetYourGuide.

blocks.html: Hot minced-pork congee with a soft-boiled egg, topped with shredded ginger and fried garlic, is an easy, comforting way to start the day. Expect to pay around 40–60 THB a bowl, and many shops serve it alongside fish rice soup and pa thong ko under the same roof.

items.name: Pa Miao Congee (Khao Takiab)
items.blurb: Smooth pork congee with a soft-boiled egg, great with pa thong ko on the side. This is the morning congee spot people around Khao Takiab stop at before work.

items.name: Pinto Fish Rice Soup (Khao Takiab)
items.blurb: Clear fish rice soup, chicken rice and congee, tucked into the Khao Takiab community near Ameson Cafe. Open morning to midday.

items.name: Clay-Pot Kao Lao (Golf View area)
items.blurb: Pork-blood soup and kao lao served in a hot clay pot with a rich broth — a good wake-up bowl. It's in the Golf View area, just before Big C Taling Chan.

blocks.html: Dim sum in Hua Hin carries the influence of the old Chinese community — har gow, steamed pork dumplings, bao buns, and pan-baked eggs in little pots. Several places in town open early and keep going into the afternoon, which suits anyone who sleeps in a bit.

items.name: Tee Heng Dim Sum (town center)
items.blurb: Hot steamed dim sum, pan eggs and bak kut teh in a herbal broth, in the center of town. Opens early and runs until around 3pm.

items.name: Coca Pop-Up (near the clock tower)
items.blurb: A comfortable sit-down spot near the Hua Hin clock tower, with congee, noodles, dim sum and fried bao. Open 7:30–21:00, closed Mondays.

blocks.html: If you want a real taste of old Hua Hin, try the traditional sock-brewed coffee — strong, brewed through a cloth bag and sweetened with condensed milk, served with pa thong ko or a sangkhaya (custard) toast. The legendary spot in this part of town is Jek Pia Coffee, a wooden shophouse going back more than 80 years.

items.name: Jek Pia Coffee
items.blurb: An old-school coffee shop in a vintage wooden building at the intersection locals call Jek Pia junction. In the morning there are carts out front selling chicken rice, red-pork and crispy-pork rice, congee and pork-blood soup, all to go with the coffee, tea and old-style Ovaltine.
items.meta: Soi Hua Hin 57, Dechanuchit Rd · 6:00–12:00 and 17:00–20:00

items.name: Coffee Carts at Chatchai Market
items.blurb: Several vendors in the morning market sell old-school coffee by the cup — sip one with a hot pa thong ko while you walk the market. Local prices.

blocks.title: For the Vintage Vibe
blocks.html: Most of the old-school coffee shops around here are family-run with limited seating, and they get busy on weekends. If you want to settle in and relax, go on a weekday or before 8am — it's much easier.

items: Start at 6:30 — walk Chatchai Market and try grilled pork, pa thong ko and soy milk, with an old-school coffee to go.
7:30 — sit down for a proper bowl at a congee shop or at Jek Pia: order pork congee with egg, or chicken rice.
8:30 — finish with hot dim sum if you still have room, before the market starts winding down.

faq.q: Where should I eat breakfast in Hua Hin?
faq.a: Start at Chatchai Market in the center of town — it has everything from grilled pork and pa thong ko to soy milk, roast duck and chicken rice. If you'd rather have the old-fashioned vibe with traditional coffee, head to Jek Pia near Soi Hua Hin 57.

faq.q: What time does Chatchai Market open, and when should I go?
faq.a: The morning market is busiest from 6am to 8am, and the best food at several stalls is gone before 9am. Go early and bring cash, since most vendors don't take cards or bank transfers.

faq.q: How much does congee cost in Hua Hin?
faq.a: Regular pork congee runs about 40–60 THB a bowl, and you can add a soft-boiled egg. Fish rice soup starts at 30 THB at some shops — local prices all around.

faq.q: Until what time can I get dim sum in Hua Hin?
faq.a: Dim sum places in town like Tee Heng open early and keep going until around 3pm. A relaxed sit-down spot like Coca Pop-Up near the clock tower is open 7:30 to 21:00, closed Mondays.

faq.q: If I don't get up super early, will there still be something to eat?
faq.a: Yes — if you sleep in a bit, go for dim sum or one of the places that stays open into the afternoon. But to get the full spread at Chatchai Market, you'll want to be there before 9am.
